pr.title: [Merged by Bors] - feat(RingTheory/WittVector): isomorphism of Witt vectors mod p with base ring
pr.body:
This resolves a TODO in the basic theory of Witt vectors, giving an isomorphism between `W(k)/p` and `k` where `k` is a perfect ring of characteristic `p`.

---

review_comments.body:
It would be useful to introduce auxiliary lemmas:
```lean
lemma ker_constantCoeff :
    RingHom.ker constantCoeff = Ideal.span {(p : 𝕎 k)} := by
  ext
  simp [mem_span_p_iff_coeff_zero_eq_zero]

-- this should be moved to the `Teichmuller` file
lemma constantCoeff_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (constantCoeff : 𝕎 k → k) :=
  fun r ↦ ⟨teichmuller p r, rfl⟩

noncomputable def quotientPEquiv :
    𝕎 k ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : 𝕎 k)} ≃+* k :=
  (Ideal.quotEquivOfEq ker_constantCoeff.symm).trans
    (RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective constantCoeff_surjective)

@[simp]
lemma quotientPEquiv_mk (x : 𝕎 k) :
    quotientPEquiv (Quot.mk _ x) = constantCoeff x := rfl
````
The most important remark about your code is that it creates data (here an isomorphism) using tactics, which in general is problematic when unfolding definitions. Above, instead of rewriting the ideal generated by `p` as a kernel, I use `Ideal.quotEquivOfEq`, which allows to prove the equational lemma `quotientPEquiv_mk`, which would not work otherwise.
